senses.gloss: m. h. (denom. of חֲמוֹר) ass-driver, attendant of beasts of burden.
units: <cite ref="Mishnah Kiddushin 4:14">Kidd. IV, 14</cite>, a. e., v. <cite ref="C01040"><he>גַּמָּל</he></cite>.

<cite ref="Mishnah Kelim 26:5">Kel. XXVI, 5</cite> (<cite ref="Mishnah Kelim 26:6">6</cite>) <he>עור החמיר ועור הח׳</he> Maim. (v. comment. ed. Dehr.; Mish. ed. <he>עור הח׳</he>, Talm. ed. <he>עור החמור</he>) the ass’ leather cover and the ass-driver’s apron; a. fr.—<he>ח׳ גמל</he>, v. <cite ref="C01040"><he>גַּמָּל</he></cite>.—Pl. <cite ref="H01203"><he>חַמָּרִים</he></cite>, <he>חַמָּרִין</he>.
Dem. IV, 7. Kidd. l. c. a. fr.—Denom.: חִמֵּר to direct a loaded beast’s motions by walking behind it, to load a beast.

<cite ref="Shabbat 153b">Sabb. 153ᵇ</cite>; <cite ref="Avodah Zarah 15a:5">Ab. Zar. 15ᵃ</cite> <he>המְחַמֵּר אחר וכ׳</he> he who drives his beast of burden by walking behind it. Sabb. l. c. <he>והלא מחמר</he> but does he not violate the Sabbath as a driver (by placing his money bag on the ass)?—
<cite ref="Pesachim 66b:4">Pes. 66ᵇ</cite> <he>מח׳ כלאחר יד הוא</he> it is an act of driving in an unusual way (the lamb usually not being used as a beast of burden); a. fr.
